style_rules: Match the prompt backdrop to the final layout ground — either pure flat #FFFFFF seamless white for cutout-on-ground or full-bleed flat Retail Purple (#340A5C) with no gradient — so pasted cutouts never show rectangular photo-box seams.

Anchor the hero subject inside explicit inset coordinates (e.g., x=9.5% to 39% for left-column layouts or x=18% to 82% for centered layouts, spanning y=10% to 82.5%) to protect the 100px top and side margins while preventing dead bottom gaps.
Attach a real product sheet whenever possible and instruct the model to match exact bottle shapes, colours, caps, packaging, and printed details, keeping labels front-facing and unobstructed.
Keep the entire hero subject and its soft contact shadow strictly inside the inset bounding box, or ground hands/stems cleanly at y=100% in full-bleed shots so nothing gets sliced mid-canvas.

Include exact brand hex codes alongside material finish and lighting (e.g., Retail Purple #340A5C, gold #D9A441, glossy patent #C90E13, eye-level studio product photograph) so purples and accents stay on-palette.
Describe clear, physically plausible studio orientations (such as tiered vertical placement, tabletop presentation, or hands cradling a product) rather than surreal object-to-object morphs.
When prompting human subjects, specify natural skin texture, warm expressions, and gentle gestures explicitly so the model preserves an upbeat gifting mood.
Omit all Kapruka logos, wordmarks, headlines, and ad typography from the image prompt so they are added cleanly in layout rather than AI-painted.
avoid: Never use a pure white (#FFFFFF) cutout ground when the final ad canvas is Retail Purple (#340A5C), and never use tinted cream (#F5F4EB) or radial vignettes, which expose visible rectangular photo-box seams.
Never instruct objects to enter from x=0% or be cropped hard off the left or top frame edge, which causes harsh vertical slices, clipped silhouettes, and top-margin violations.
Never ask the model to paint Kapruka wordmarks or logos onto bags, products, or the background, which causes uneven letterforms, ghost duplicates, or logos on sellable goods.
Avoid rendering tiny, intricate printed brand text on small or distant product labels without clear front-facing framing, which causes AI-garbled lettering.

Avoid complex object-to-object morphing devices (such as heels, straps, or globe arcs turning into molten liquid, prongs, or ribbons), which trigger warped shapes, missing elements, and broken composition scale.
Never let soft ground shadows bleed past the cutout bounds, which produces visible straight horizontal or vertical cuts across the shadow.
Avoid vague floating compositions or omitting clear surface grounding, which correlates with grey rectangular ghost patches and placeholder boxes.
Do not end hero artwork high on the canvas (around 48% to 65% height) or tuck the payoff small in a corner, which creates top-heavy dead white zones and unreadable thumbnails.
Do not rely on generic colour names like deep purple without hex values, which frequently render as off-brand grey-violet.
Avoid negative action words like frown or protest for human subjects, as models exaggerate them into genuine anger or shouting.
lessons.structure: Open with shot type (eye-level studio product photograph), 4:5 portrait aspect ratio, and a seamless flat ground matching the layout canvas (#FFFFFF for cutout-on-ground with no border, horizon, or panel seams, or full-bleed flat #340A5C Retail Purple with no vignette). Define an explicit inset placement box (e.g., x=9.5%–39% or x=18%–82%, y=10%–82.5%) and specify physically plausible subject orientation, real-product-sheet fidelity with clear front-facing labels, exact hex colours, material finish, and a fully contained contact shadow. Close with clean studio lighting and warm mood cues while strictly excluding any Kapruka logos, ad typography, edge-cropping, or shape-morphing gimmicks.
